problem_text:
A courier must traverse a network of 7 regional distribution hubs to collect time-sensitive financial documents.

The travel times between hubs, measured in minutes, are precisely as follows:
* Hub Alpha to Hub Beta: 169.4 minutes
* Hub Alpha to Hub Gamma: 47.2 minutes
* Hub Alpha to Hub Delta: 19.4 minutes
* Hub Alpha to Hub Epsilon: 188.3 minutes
* Hub Alpha to Hub Zeta: 51.6 minutes
* Hub Alpha to Hub Eta: 71.7 minutes
* Hub Beta to Hub Gamma: 175.8 minutes
* Hub Beta to Hub Delta: 159.2 minutes
* Hub Beta to Hub Epsilon: 43.0 minutes
* Hub Beta to Hub Zeta: 117.7 minutes
* Hub Beta to Hub Eta: 104.1 minutes
* Hub Gamma to Hub Delta: 64.1 minutes
* Hub Gamma to Hub Epsilon: 184.1 minutes
* Hub Gamma to Hub Zeta: 69.6 minutes
* Hub Gamma to Hub Eta: 72.0 minutes
* Hub Delta to Hub Epsilon: 182.0 minutes
* Hub Delta to Hub Zeta: 43.9 minutes
* Hub Delta to Hub Eta: 69.1 minutes
* Hub Epsilon to Hub Zeta: 138.2 minutes
* Hub Epsilon to Hub Eta: 117.3 minutes
* Hub Zeta to Hub Eta: 27.9 minutes

The objective is to ascertain the minimal-duration circuit that permits the courier to arrive at each hub exactly once before concluding the journey at the initial point of departure.
